kernelIdea: a + bi is plotted at (a,b) on a plane with real horizontal axis and imaginary vertical axis. Addition is the parallelogram rule; conjugation is reflection in the real axis.

kernels.l1: Walk across, then walk up. Mark the spot. That is the number.
kernels.l2: Every complex number is a spot on a grid: go across for the first part, up for the second. Adding two of them means doing one walk and then the other.
kernels.l3: Plot a + bi at the point a across and b up. Adding complex numbers is joining the two walks nose to tail, and conjugating is reflecting in the horizontal axis.
kernels.l4: a + bi is the point (a, b) in the plane. Addition is the parallelogram rule, conjugation is reflection in the real axis — which is why the reals, lying on that axis, are fixed — and multiplication by i is a quarter turn.
kernels.l5: The complex plane makes addition vector addition and conjugation reflection; multiplication by i is rotation by a quarter turn, verified algebraically.
kernels.l6: The complex numbers are the coordinate plane with the same addition. What is new is a multiplication, and its geometric content is rotation together with scaling.
kernels.l7: Identifying a + bi with (a,b) makes addition vector addition, conjugation reflection in the real axis, and multiplication by i rotation by π/2; the geometry explains the algebra rather than illustrating it.
kernels.l8: The plane model realises ℂ as a two-dimensional real vector space with a compatible multiplication; the rotation picture is the first sight of the action of the unit circle on ℂ.

kernel: a + bi is plotted at (a,b) on a plane with a real horizontal axis and imaginary vertical axis. Addition is the parallelogram rule; conjugation is reflection in the real axis.
objectives: Explain why real numbers are fixed by conjugation
